facts.raw_span: intermittent fever
unintentional weight loss
progressive lip swelling with painful ulcerations
his CD4 count rising from 94 to 160 cells/mm3
undetectable HIV viral load
undetectable hepatitis C viral load
no hepatosplenomegaly
a polymerase‐chain‐reaction assay for herpes simplex virus from an ulcer base was negative
Complement C1 esterase inhibitor levels were within normal limits
Gram stain, acid‐fast stain, and mucicarmine stain of lesion samples were negative
Fungal blood cultures and both urine and serum Histoplasma antigen tests were negative
lips were markedly edematous, with multiple superficial ulcers having heaped‐up margins

concepts.why: The patient's lip swelling and ulcerations, combined with normal Complement C1 esterase inhibitor levels, suggest acquired angioedema.
The patient's symptoms developed after the initiation of antiretroviral therapy, which is consistent with IRIS.
The patient's lip swelling and ulcerations are consistent with cheilitis.
The patient's lip ulcerations, combined with negative herpes simplex virus PCR, suggest an oral ulcer of unknown etiology.
The patient's HIV infection and immune system dysfunction are consistent with HIV-associated immune dysfunction.
The patient has an undetectable hepatitis C viral load, indicating clearance of the virus.

rationales.F03: Lip swelling with painful ulcerations is a key feature of cheilitis and oral ulcer, making them more likely.
rationales.F04: Rising CD4 count suggests improving immune function, which could contribute to IRIS.
rationales.F05: Undetectable HIV viral load indicates well-controlled HIV infection, making HIV-associated immune dysfunction less likely.
rationales.F06: Undetectable hepatitis C viral load suggests hepatitis C clearance, which is a positive outcome.
rationales.F08: Negative herpes simplex virus PCR reduces the likelihood of cheilitis and oral ulcer being caused by herpes simplex.
rationales.F09: Normal Complement C1 esterase inhibitor levels make acquired angioedema less likely.
rationales.F12: Markedly edematous lips with multiple superficial ulcers having heaped-up margins are characteristic of cheilitis and oral ulcer.
